english_description: The scalar ChaCha20 stream cipher block function and bounded keystream operation.

queries.english: Return one 64-byte ChaCha20 block for this key nonce and counter.
queries.rust_sig: fn block(&self, key: [u8; 32], nonce: [u8; 12], counter: u32) -> [u8; 64]

queries.english: Return the number of keystream bytes remaining before counter exhaustion.

commands.english: Apply the next ChaCha20 keystream bytes to input and return the output.
commands.rust_sig: fn apply_keystream(&mut self, input: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError>

constraints.english: A ChaCha20 block contains exactly sixty-four output bytes.
A successful keystream application preserves the input length.
The requested input fits in the remaining counter stream.
A stream started at block counter c has (2^32 - c) * 64 keystream bytes available.
constraints.logic: ChaCha20::with_counter(key, nonce, counter).bytes_remaining() as u64 == (4294967296 - counter as u64) * 64

constraints.english: The remaining capacity drops by exactly the input length after a successful keystream application and is unchanged after a rejected one.
constraints.logic: match self.apply_keystream(input) { Ok(_) => self.bytes_remaining() == old(self.bytes_remaining()) - input.len(), Err(_) => self.bytes_remaining() == old(self.bytes_remaining()) }

adversary_table.scenario: Process input lengths 1, 63, 64, and 65 across block boundaries.
adversary_table.resolution: preserve the input length in every successful output

adversary_table.scenario: Request more bytes than remain before the 32-bit block counter is exhausted.
adversary_table.resolution: return a counter exhaustion error without wrapping

adversary_table.scenario: Use an all-zero key and nonce with counter zero.
adversary_table.resolution: match the pinned RFC ChaCha20 block result

adversary_table.scenario: Start streams at counters 0, 1, and 2^32 - 1 and query the remaining capacity.
adversary_table.resolution: report exactly the remaining whole-block capacity for the starting counter

adversary_table.scenario: Consume 1, 63, 64, and 65 bytes, including an overlong request near counter exhaustion, then query the remaining capacity.
adversary_table.resolution: lower the capacity by exactly the consumed length and leave it unchanged on rejection

source_references.notes: Scalar quarter-round and block path; optimized providers are separate.
